newsitem.title: PERU: Peru shrs end slightly higher on apathetic trade.
newsitem.headline: Peru shrs end slightly higher on apathetic trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima Stock Exchange closed up slightly Tuesday in low volume, as investors selectively traded stocks with good prospects, brokers said.
They expected trade to remain thin Wednesday.
Tuesday, the General Index rose 0.26 percent to 2021.72 points as the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.12 percent to 2905.43 points.
In a total of 1,820 operations, volume was 30 million soles ($11.3 million).

"The market is showing itself very quiet ... Foreigners prefer the Mexican bolsa with its higher profitability," said Arlen Lahura from local Interlima brokerage. "However, local investors are buying cheap stocks with good prospects."
Investors were also waiting for the publication of macroeconomic indicators in Brazil late Tuesday, as trade in Lima is influenced by regional trends.
Analysts added that Peru's 8.2 percent year-over-year growth in June, and 7.4 percent year-over-year growth in the first half -- announced mid-session -- had much less impact then expected.
"The June national economic growth was superior to the estimated seven percent, but the market did not respond as expected," said Hernando Pasto from local T&J brokerage.
Market leader Telefonica del Peru fell 1.11 percent to 6.24 soles on volume of 1.45 million shares.

The biggest winner among leaders was miner Volcan which rose 10.02 percent to 21.41 soles on volume of 140,000 shares, followed by cement producer Cementos Lima, which rose 5.66 percent to 5.60 soles on volume of 31,086 shares.
The construction sector recorded the greatest year-over- year growth during June and the first half of 1997.

Losers today included electricity distributor Edelnor, which fell 4.57 percent to 1.67 soles on volume of 26,120 shares, and miner Morococha, which fell 2.14 percent to 6.85 soles on volume of 55,254 shares.
